cosmopedia.orbitcore.earth.title: Earth
cosmopedia.orbitcore.earth.text: The third planet from the Sun and, so far, the only known home of life. The space program starts here: metals, fuel and the first rockets are all made on Earth. Gravity is 1 g, and everything that goes to space has to be pushed against it.
cosmopedia.orbitcore.moon.title: The Moon
cosmopedia.orbitcore.moon.text: Earth's only natural satellite. Gravity is six times weaker than on Earth and there is no air, so a spacesuit is required on the surface. The dark patches are lunar seas of frozen basalt; the bright areas are ancient highlands. Polar craters that never see the Sun may hide water ice. Observers sometimes report a strange glint inside one of the craters that neither sunlight nor ice can explain.
cosmopedia.orbitcore.bauxite.title: Bauxite
cosmopedia.orbitcore.bauxite.text: A rusty sedimentary rock and the main ore of aluminum. Aluminum is bound to oxygen too tightly to be smelted in a furnace, so it takes electrolysis. Light and strong, aluminum will become the backbone of rocket hulls.
cosmopedia.orbitcore.rutile.title: Rutile
cosmopedia.orbitcore.rutile.text: Dark red needle crystals of titanium dioxide, found deep underground. Titanium withstands heat and loads that break steel, which is why engines and spacesuits are made of it. It only smelts at very high temperatures.
cosmopedia.orbitcore.silicon.title: Silicon
cosmopedia.orbitcore.silicon.text: Made from sand or quartz in the Metallurgical Furnace. Without silicon there are no circuit boards, solar panels or flight computers. Every rocket needs a brain, and that brain is made of silicon.

cosmopedia.orbitcore.regolith.title: Regolith
cosmopedia.orbitcore.regolith.text: Lunar dust ground up by billions of years of meteorite impacts. Sharp as broken glass and clingy with static. There is no wind on the Moon, so footprints in regolith last forever. It hides helium-3, the fuel of future fusion reactors.
cosmopedia.orbitcore.ilmenite.title: Ilmenite
cosmopedia.orbitcore.ilmenite.text: A black, shiny mineral from the lunar seas: iron, titanium and oxygen. It can give a lunar base its metal and, one day, its breathing oxygen.
cosmopedia.orbitcore.lunar_ice.title: Lunar Ice
cosmopedia.orbitcore.lunar_ice.text: The Sun never rises in the craters near the poles, and water ice has gathered there for billions of years. Water is drink, oxygen and hydrogen fuel. Whoever holds the ice holds the Moon.
